concepts.definition: The status of the award as reported in the notice (awards[0].status), expressed with the OCDS award status codelist and 'unknown' for anything not published. It is a separate claim from the contract status because OCDS defines distinct award and contract codelists; where both are published they are recorded independently rather than collapsed.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.contract.status is the contract's own status from the OCDS contract codelist; entity.status is the business's registration status. Neither can carry an award status without asserting a different entity's or a different codelist's meaning.

concepts.definition: The date the award was made as stated in the notice (awards[0].date), with the published time component dropped. It is the award decision date, not the contract signature date, the contract period start, or the release publication date.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.contract.signed_date is when the contract was signed, dyn.contract.start_date is the first day of the contract term, and observation.observed_at is when the source stated the record. None of these is the award decision date.

concepts.definition: The publisher's award identifier within the release (awards[0].id, e.g. CN4280221-da775ca26c734f5eb2c07b501f71fb5c). It is a release-local join key from contract to award, not a business identifier and not stable across sources.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.contract.notice_number is the contract notice identifier, not the award identifier; entity.abn and entity.acn identify the business. No existing concept holds an award-scoped reference.

concepts.definition: The publisher's identifier for a contracted item within the release (contracts[0].items[0].id). It is an internal item key local to the release, not a business identifier, and exists only to keep the item classification claim traceable to its item.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.contract.notice_number identifies the notice, not an item; dyn.contract.item_classification_code holds the classification code but not the item's own key, so the item cannot be traced without a separate reference.

concepts.definition: The title string published for the contract (contracts[0].title), kept verbatim as stated. In this snapshot it holds short agency reference strings (e.g. NCD11811) rather than descriptive titles, so it is recorded as a stated reference and never interpreted as a description of the work.
concepts.why_not_existing: dyn.contract.description holds the scope-of-work text, which is a different field with different meaning; dyn.contract.notice_number is the notice identifier. Neither can carry the publisher's title string without conflating it with a description or an identifier.

reuse.entity.legal_name: OCDS parties[].name is the single party name the publisher states for the supplier and for the procuring entity, so it is the entity's name attribute. The publisher does not distinguish registered from trading names, so the value is recorded as stated and no legal form is inferred from forms such as 'The Trustee for ... Trust' or 'Data#3 Limited'.
reuse.entity.abn: parties[].additionalIdentifiers[] where scheme is AU-ABN carries an 11-digit ABN for both the supplier party and the procuring entity party; entity.abn already exists and requires checksum validation rather than length checks. An ABN is an identifier only and proves nothing about legal form.
reuse.address.locality: parties[].address.locality is the suburb or locality of the party's own stated address, which is exactly what address.locality holds for a business.
reuse.address.state: parties[].address.region values are Australian state and territory abbreviations (NT, QLD, VIC, ACT) matching the address.state enum. ext.entity.operating_region is not used because a stated address region is not a claimed service footprint.
reuse.address.postcode: parties[].address.postalCode is the postal code of the party's stated address, matching address.postcode.
reuse.address.country: parties[].address.countryName is the country of the party's stated address as written (AUSTRALIA, COLOMBIA, SWITZERLAND, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES), which is what address.country stores.
reuse.observation.source_record_id: releases[].id identifies exactly one published release, which is the row grain, so it is the natural traceable record key for observation.source_record_id.
reuse.observation.observed_at: releases[].date is the publication timestamp of the notice, i.e. when the source stated this record; it is not valid_from and not the contract start date.
reuse.observation.source_id: The catalogue metadata gives a stable dataset identity (austender_new) for these notices, which is what observation.source_id is for.
reuse.observation.licence: The dataset metadata declares the CC-BY 3.0 Australia licence, which observation.licence records directly from the publisher.
reuse.ext.contact.role_email: parties[].contactPoint.email publishes role mailboxes (procurement@niaa.gov.au, tenders@finance.gov.au); the concept already stores role mailboxes and drops personal ones.
reuse.ext.contact.phone: parties[].contactPoint.telephone values are Australian numbers to be normalised to E.164; the concept already encodes the area-code rule and the mobile-as-personal-data caution.
reuse.dyn.contract.notice_number: contracts[0].id is the publisher's contract notice identifier (e.g. CN4280221) and is already modelled as the contract's notice number; it is not a supplier key, ABN or ACN.
reuse.dyn.contract.signed_date: contracts[0].dateSigned is the date the contract was signed as stated in the notice; the published time component is a publication artefact and is dropped. It is not the contract start date, the notice publication date, or the business's registration date.
reuse.dyn.contract.start_date: contracts[0].period.startDate is the first day of the contract period stated in the notice; it is the start of this contract's term, not the release publication date and not the moment the notice was observed.
reuse.dyn.contract.end_date: contracts[0].period.endDate is the last day of the contract period stated in the notice, i.e. the planned end of this contract's term. It is not a licence expiry and not a business's cessation.
reuse.dyn.contract.description: contracts[0].description is the scope of work as the procuring entity described it; it is source-stated activity text describing this procurement, not the supplier's company-wide industry or sector.
reuse.dyn.contract.value: contracts[0].value.amount is the total maximum value of the contract over its life as reported in the notice, qualified by the published ISO 4217 currency. It is not annual expenditure, not revenue or business income.
reuse.dyn.contract.value_currency: contracts[0].value.currency is the ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code published with the contract value, so the currency qualifier on dyn.contract.value is always explicit and the amount is never read unqualified.
reuse.dyn.contract.status: contracts[0].status is the contract status as reported in the notice at extraction time, expressed with the OCDS contract status codelist and 'unknown' for anything not published. It is not the supplier's registration status.
reuse.dyn.contract.item_classification_code: contracts[0].items[0].classification.id is the classification code of a contracted item as published, always paired with the publisher's scheme (here UNSPSC). The code describes the goods or services bought under this contract, not the supplier's company-wide industry.
reuse.dyn.contract.procurement_method: tender.procurementMethod is how the contract was let as reported in the notice, expressed with the OCDS procurement method codelist and 'unknown' if not published. It describes the procurement process only and says nothing about contract size, supplier capability or the notice population.
reuse.dyn.contract.limited_tender_exempt: tender.limitedTenderExempt is whether the notice marks the limited tender as exempt, published as 1 or 0 and mapped to true/false; a blank value is 'unknown', never false. It records a stated procurement exemption, not a judgement about whether the exemption was justified.
reuse.dyn.contract.limited_tender_reason_code: tender.limitedTenderReasonCode is the exemption clause code the publisher gives for a limited tender (e.g. TR, AD), kept as stated. The code refers to a Commonwealth procurement exemption clause, which the verbatim reason text quotes.
reuse.dyn.contract.limited_tender_reason: tender.limitedTenderReason is the publisher's full wording of the reason a limited tender was used, kept verbatim as source evidence with its clause numbering and headings. It is a reported justification, not an assessment made by us.

unmapped.reason: roles is the discriminator used to bind supplier_party and procuring_entity_party; its meaning is already carried by the CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY relationships, so a separate role claim would duplicate them.
roles is the discriminator used to bind the procuring entity party; its meaning is already carried by CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY, so a separate role claim would duplicate it.

An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning. ABN is the published identifier where available, and a source-specific party key concept would duplicate identity without adding evidence; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.
An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.

ocid identifies an OCDS contracting process or package that can span multiple releases, awards and contracts, not a single contract or supplier. At this one-release-per-row grain the release id already keys the record and there is no contracting-process entity type.
tender.id repeats the ocid in this snapshot, so it is a process-level key rather than a tender or contract identifier.
A human-readable restatement of procurementMethod ('Limited tender', 'Open tender'); storing both would create a redundant alias of dyn.contract.procurement_method.

A local join key from contract to award inside the release, not a business fact; the supplier link it supports is already recorded by CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and the award itself by dyn.contract.award_reference.
A denormalised restatement of parties[].name for the same supplier; mapping both would double-count one name claim.

contactPoint.name mixes organisational unit labels ('FINANCE DIVISION', 'Procurement') with personal names ('Sandra Tuck'). The ontology has no concept for a contact's unit, and personal names must not be stored, so these are dropped rather than mapped.
A contact organisational branch label for the party, not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology; it is also mixed with agency names rather than branches.
A contact organisational division label for the party, not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology; it is also mixed with agency names rather than divisions.
A single street-address line (e.g. 'PO Box 3'), often a post-office box. address.full expects a complete formatted address and concatenating lines would invent structure the source does not state.
A single street-address line for a government agency; the same objection as for supplier street addresses applies, and address.full is not a street-line concept.
Not present in the inspected bindings for the procuring entity party; the column profile shows no nonempty values, so no country claim can be made without inventing data.
Not present in the inspected bindings for the procuring entity party; no phone claim can be made without inventing data.
Constant ('contract') schema metadata describing the OCDS release stage, not a business fact; the contract entity already carries that meaning.
Constant ('tender') OCDS schema metadata describing how the process was initiated, with no business fact about the supplier or the contract.
A document language tag ('EN') for the release payload, not a claim about any business or contract.
